more.title: South Africa’s Orange Basin Gains Momentum as Navitas Takes Block 1 CBK Operatorship
more.description: Following regulatory approval from the South African government, Navitas Petroleum has assumed operatorship of Block 1 CBK offshore South Africa. This follows Eco Atlantic's completion of a farm-down of a 37.5% working interest in the license to Navitas. The deal provides the Atlantic Margins explorer's partner with one of the Orange Basin's largest exploration blocks. The frontier region has drawn major industry players including Shell, TotalEnergies, bp, and Galp since play-opening discoveries offshore Namibia started transforming the area's upstream landscape in 2022. The African Energy Chamber (AEC) welcomes the completion of Eco (Atlantic) Oil&Gas’ farm-down in Block 1 CBK. As the voice of the African energy sector, the Chamber views the transaction as an important step in advancing exploration and unlocking the country’s significant offshore oil and gas potential. Completed on September 22 following South African regulatory approvals, the transaction transfers operatorship of the 19,929-km 2 block to Navitas. Eco retains a 37.5% interest, while local partner OrangeBasin Energies maintains 25%. Eco received $4 million in cash and will be carried by Navitas for up to $7.5 million of its share of the work program. Block 1 CBK sits within the Orange Basin, one of Africa’s most active frontier exploration areas, directly adjacent to Namibia and close to recent discoveries by Galp Energia, TotalEnergies, Rhino Resources and Shell. Three legacy wells have already confirmed a gas discovery with tested flow rates of 32.4 million standard cubic feet per day. “South Africa has an opportunity to turn its offshore resource potential into investment, energy security, jobs and economic growth,” says NJ Ayuk, Executive Chairman, AEC. “Partnerships that combine international capital and technical expertise with local participation can help move these resources toward development while creating wider opportunities across the African energy value chain.” An August 2026 review by Eco and Navitas estimated more than 3.6 billion barrels of unrisked prospective oil resources and approximately 4.5 trillion cubic feet of prospective gas resources on Block 1 CBK. The partners are continuing advanced interpretation and reprocessing of existing seismic data to identify prospects and potential drilling targets, with the farm-down carrying Eco’s share of a work program that includes two planned exploration wells. The transaction also demonstrates how farm-downs can distribute exploration risk while preserving exposure to high-impact African resources. Navitas assumes operational responsibility and expenditure commitments, while Eco retains substantial upside. If the existing option with OrangeBasin Energies is exercised in full and Navitas acquires half of the additional interest, Eco and Navitas would each hold 47.5% with OrangeBasin Energies retaining 5%. For South Africa, successful exploration could support domestic oil and gas supply, attract international investment and generate demand for local services, technology and expertise. The project also forms part of a broader Orange Basin exploration story spanning South Africa and Namibia, reinforcing the region’s growing importance within Africa’s upstream landscape. The AEC supports continued collaboration between government, international operators, African companies and financial and technical partners to advance Block 1 CBK. As Navitas assumes operatorship, the project provides an opportunity to convert substantial geological potential into exploration activity, investment and, ultimately, energy and economic value for South Africa and the continent. Distributed by APO Group on behalf of African Energy Chamber.

more.title: South Africa strikes gold with nine gold medals at Tug-of-War World Championships in Mossel Bay
more.description: Western Cape Minister of Cultural Affairs and Sport, Ricardo Mackenzie, has congratulated South Africa’s athletes on securing fifteen medals, including nine gold, at the 30th Tug-of-War World Championships. The championships concluded this weekend in Hartenbos, Mossel Bay The tournament featured national teams and clubs from sixteen countries. The championships returned to the Western Cape eight years after Cape Town hosted the Outdoor World Championships in 2018. The Western Cape Department of Cultural Affairs and Sport (DCAS) invested R1.5 million in the championships, following two years of planning and partnership. This investment forms part of the Western Cape Government’s commitment to strengthening sporting pathways from school to club, to provincial and national colours, and onto the world stage, alongside its R130 million school sport strategy over three years. The championship week opened on Wednesday, 16 September with the TWIF Open Club Championships, followed by the World Championships on 18 and 19 September, when athletes competed in their national colours. The competition spanned junior, under-23 and senior weight categories. South Africa’s medal tally for the championship week was as follows: World Open Club Championships: five gold and two silver medals. World Championships – National Teams: four gold, two silver, and two bronze medals. This brings South Africa’s combined total to nine gold, four silver and two bronze medals. South African club gold medallists included Hartenbos in the Under-23 Men’s 600kg, Goudini in the Under-23 Women’s 500kg, Drostdy A in Junior Men’s 560kg, Robertson High School in Junior Mixed 520kg, and Valsbaai A in Under-23 Mixed 560kg. Swellendam and Valsbaai B secured silver medals in their weight categories. South Africa’s national teams claimed gold in the Junior Men 560kg, Under-23 Men 600kg, Under-23 Mixed 560kg, and Senior Men 600kg. This also includes silver in Junior Women 480kg and senior mixed 580kg, and bronze in the Senior Men 680kg and Under-23 Women 500kg. Adding to these achievements, Kittie Terblanche from South Africa was named the TWIF Female Outdoor Athlete of the Year, following a public voting process. Reflecting on the championships, Minister Mackenzie said, “What I saw this week was not just competition. I saw the professionalism of the athletes and officials, the commitment of the organisers, the pride of teams representing their countries, and the warmth of the entire tug-of-war community. To our South African clubs and national teams: baie geluk! To win fifteen medals, including nine gold, against some of the world’s best on home soil is an outstanding achievement.” The championships also generated significant public interest online with Minister Mackenzie’s TikTok videos attracting more than half a million views. Audiences asked where they could watch more competitions and how they could get involved. “When you give a sport the platform it deserves, people respond. I certainly see an opportunity to promote tug-of-war more, share more of these incredible moments, and introduce the sport to people who have never experienced it before”, said Mackenzie. At the farewell ceremony held on 19 September, President of the Tug-of-War International Federation (TWIF), Mr Dan McCarthy (Ireland), acknowledged the Western Cape Government’s support for the championships. “Minister, thank you for your financial contribution, and I hope you will continue to support tug-of-war,” said McCarthy. Minister Mackenzie also thanked the South African Tug-of-War Federation and its President, Mr Luther Anton Botha, Convenor of the Selection Panel, Mr Carel Moller, the Local Organising Committee, the officials, volunteers, and everyone who contributed to the successful hosting of the championships. “What an incredible World Tug-of-War Championships! With eight medals secured in the World Championships, including four golds, our athletes and officials have demonstrated remarkable dedication, determination and teamwork. Behind the success of this event stands an exceptional team of volunteers who have given their time, passion and energy so generously. Their commitment reminds us that, together, we truly pull stronger,” stated Mr Botha. The championships placed Mossel Bay and the Western Cape firmly on the international sporting map, demonstrating the province’s capacity to host world-class sporting events, inspiring young athletes across the province that the journey to the world stage can begin right here. The opportunity now is to grow participation, build on the enthusiasm generated in Hartenbos, and to ensure that the legacy of these championships extends beyond the final pull. Distributed by APO Group on behalf of Western Cape Government: Office of the Premier.
